liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Garcia's lead playing on Shakedown Street is blazing and makes the tape essential; Reviewer considers this Shakedown Street unbeatable among all versions [15][20][21]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): Reviewer says this He's Gone smokes; Reviewer calls this He's Gone one for the ages, with breathtaking beauty [24][25]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Reviewer hears this opener as fast and lively, with a plucky feel [22]
- **Good Time Blues** (1 review): Brent is praised on Good Time Blues, and Garcia's soloing is said to wail [26]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Brent's piano solo on Iko Iko as superb [24]
- **Throwin' Stones** (1 review): Reviewer points to Throwin' Stones as the real standout, urging listeners to hear it [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Smokestack/Spoonful Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-03-30.134853.bltz.flac2496** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 146 min [1]
- **gd87-03-30.matrix.18255.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 144 min; rated 4.24/5 by 25 [2]. Said about its sound: Sounds excellent because it is a soundboard recording with audience sound blended in; Reviewer praises the balanced mix of audience and soundboard sources; Reviewer's copy had a defect that made The Other One inaudible, though Throwin' Stones came through strongly [17][19][26]
- **gd1987-03-30.sbd-mtx.clugston.tetzeli.fix-18255.34394.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 144 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd1987-03-30.163486.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 147 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1987-03-30.167565.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 148 min [8]
- **gd87-03-30.nak.braverman.10922.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 139 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [13]. Said about its sound: Sounds excellent because it is a soundboard recording with audience sound blended in [18]

## Around the show

- Box of Rain draws an approving response from the crowd, according to the reviewer [22]
- Reviewer claims no other first set is tighter or more consistent than this one [20]
- Reviewer slightly prefers the 3/29 show over this one, though this is still good [22]
- Reviewer ranks this He's Gone alongside the Nassau 1981 version, 'Bobby Sands' [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-03-30.134853.bltz.flac2496**: taped by bltz; transferred by bltz; source: Source: Nakamichi CM-300s/Shotguns -> Sony Walkman Pro/Maxell MX 90 -> JVC TD-W354 -> Zoom H6 96/24 WAV -> Audacity -> FLAC 96/24 [1]
- **gd87-03-30.matrix.18255.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette (Ultr-Matrix Mix) > Reel to Reel > PCM > CDR [2]
- **gd1987-03-30.sbd-mtx.clugston.tetzeli.fix-18255.34394.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Bill Tetzeli; source: MSC (Ultra-Matrix) > Reel to Reel > PCM > CDR [4]. Also: Bill removed the gap between disc 2 and disc 3 tracks; the fixed SBEs were verified with shntool [4]
- **gd1987-03-30.163486.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME80 mics > Sony D5M [7]. Also: A 0:40 patch in Space comes from Miller's ultramatrix source; Joe D'Amico's Nakamichi 300 source supplies the final 3:15 of the encore [7]
- **gd1987-03-30.167565.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [8]. Also: Hessberg's Sennheiser ME-80 source supplies 0:19 of crowd and the first notes of Cassidy [8]
- **gd87-03-30.nak.braverman.10922.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Master Cassette (Nak 300/Sony D5) [13]
